# Phase 1 tasks — song identity and the Wanted list

Each task is sized for one cheap-worker run (≤ ~10 files, ≤ ~400 lines of diff; see `AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`). The full spec for each lives in `docs/build/tasks/<id>.md` (from `WORKER_TASK_TEMPLATE.md`) and is committed on `main` before its worker starts. Tasks without a shared dependency run in parallel worktrees. External API facts were verified live on 2026-09-28 (`docs/research/research_metadata_plex.md` §1.2.1); recorded responses live under `tests/fixtures/{musicbrainz,deezer,itunes}/`.

| ID | Title | Depends on | Size | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1-01 | Domain model and seeds: `artist`, `song`, `song_artist`, `album_context`, `song_file`, `quality` (seeded, stable ids), `quality_profile` ("Standard 320", "Lossless"), default `library`; migration; cutoff logic; repository tests | — | M | worker |
| P1-02 | MusicBrainz client + metadata plumbing: per-host rate-limit handler (1 req/s), resilience with `Retry-After`, `metadata_cache` table + cache service with TTLs, recording search / lookup / ISRC / release browse / release lookup; contract tests on recorded fixtures; opt-in live test | — | M | worker |

| P1-07 | Song add service (Core): artist upsert, batch album planning, track numbers from the chosen release, one cover per album, song/artist queries, per-song album override | P1-01, P1-04, P1-05, P1-06, P1-10 | M | worker |

Waves: **A** P1-01 ∥ P1-02 ∥ P1-03 → **B** P1-04 ∥ P1-05 ∥ P1-08 ∥ P1-10 → **C** P1-06 ∥ P1-12 → P1-07 → P1-07b → **D** P1-09 → P1-11 → **E** P1-13. (P1-07 was split into Core service + API on 2026-09-28 to keep each diff reviewable.)

Tasks that add a migration (P1-01, P1-02, P1-09, P1-10) may run in parallel; the second to merge gets its migration regenerated by the orchestrator (`dotnet ef migrations remove` on the branch, merge, `dotnet ef migrations add`) so the model snapshot stays linear.

## Design decisions taken for Phase 1 (recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, Build session 2)

- **Identity chain for free text:** Deezer search (plain `q=`, filtered client-side) supplies an ISRC and a reference duration; MB `/isrc/{isrc}` then names the recording. Without an ISRC hit, MB recording search candidates are ranked on title, artist, version flags and duration against the Deezer reference. Deezer-only songs are kept (`deezer_id`, no MBID); nothing found → the line is "unresolved".
- **Releases for the album policy** come from MB's release browse (`/release?recording=`, official, ≤ 3 pages of 100), because recording lookups cap `inc=releases` at 25; the track/disc number is read from one release lookup of the chosen release only.
- **Quality profile items** are an ordered (worst → best) list of groups; a file meets the cutoff when its group is at or above the cutoff quality's group, so "AAC-256 counts as met" is expressed by putting AAC-256 in the MP3-320 group.
- **Pseudo-album** title is `Singles` (album artist = the artist), one synthetic UUID per artist, one date fixed at creation; the `compilation` policy uses one `Various Artists` album per library titled with the library name.
- **Pasted lists** are stored as an import list of type `paste` so the unresolved-review state is the one Phase 6 import lists will reuse.
- **Deezer previews** are signed and expire (~30 min), so they are never stored: the UI asks `GET /api/v1/preview` for a fresh URL.
